stem: A form marks required fields with a red asterisk only. What is the most accessible fix?

options.text: Add the word 'required' to each label and set the `required` attribute.
options.rationale: A visible word plus the required attribute conveys the requirement in text and in code, not by color alone.

options.text: Add a legend at the top explaining that red means required.
options.rationale: A legend depends on readers noticing and remembering it, the field itself still relies on color.
A placeholder disappears once the user types and is not a reliable label.

options.text: Make the asterisk larger and brighter red.
options.rationale: A stronger color is still a color-only cue and does not help people who cannot see it.

explanation: Required status should be available in text and in markup. Put 'required' in the label (or provide an equivalent instruction) and set the `required` attribute so browsers and assistive technology expose the state. A red asterisk, a legend, a placeholder, or a brighter color does not give every reader the same information.

references.title: W3C WAI — Forms Tutorial: Form Instructions
